message.text:
The frontend interceptor lives at `web/src/connect.ts` as `authInterceptor`. It manages an access token sent as a Bearer header via `localStorage` through `auth-state.ts`, and a refresh token stored in an HttpOnly cookie consumed by a `refreshToken` RPC call with `credentials: include`. The backend package that validates these tokens is `server/auth`, containing `authenticator.go` and `token.go`.

A second interceptor, `NewAuthInterceptor`, exists in the API v1 layer. It relies on `Authorizer`, which also consumes `server/auth`.

message.text:
The frontend interceptor manages two tokens. The access token is a Bearer Authorization header stored in localStorage via auth-state. The refresh token is an HttpOnly cookie sent via credentials: include on the refreshToken RPC.

The interceptor lives at web/src/connect.ts. The backend package that validates these tokens is server/auth.

q29.
web/src/connect.ts; access token (Bearer) and refresh token (HttpOnly cookie); server/auth

`authInterceptor` attaches `Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>` (storage in `web/src/auth-state.ts`) and on 401/expiry calls `AuthService.refreshToken` with `credentials: "include"`. The backend validates tokens in `server/auth` (`authenticator.go`, `token.go`); Connect/gateway use `Authorizer` in `server/router/api/v1/authz.go`. PATs are validated there too but are not what the frontend interceptor manages.
